sections.html:
East central Indiana, right on the Ohio line, is where Wayne County sits. Richmond is the seat and biggest city. Centerville, Cambridge City, Hagerstown, Dalton, Pennville and Fountain City are among the smaller towns. Total area is about 404 square miles.

July 2025 brought a population estimate of 66,169. That is 0.6% under the 2020 base and well under the 68,917 counted in 2010. The county holds 30,804 housing units and 26,975 households, and owners live in 69.2% of homes. A typical owner-occupied home is worth $140,200, a typical rent is $815 and the median household income is $55,692. The county issued 271 building permits in 2025.

Richmond's historic districts contain many older houses that need steady upkeep. Roofs, furnaces and foundations absorb the worst of Indiana's seasonal swings, and the cost of repairs pushes some owners to sell as-is.

Each parcel gets its value from the Wayne County Assessor, whose office is on the lower level of the Wayne County Administration Building at 301 E. Main St. in Richmond. Beacon, the Schneider online records site, shows the assessed value of any parcel.

An owner who disagrees with the value follows Indiana's general appeal rule, which uses Form 130:

  • The deadline is June 15 of the year that matches your notice. In 2025 Wayne County's date was June 16, so check the date printed on yours.
  • Every parcel needs its own petition.
  • The PTABOA must schedule a hearing within 180 days.
  • If the PTABOA ruling is unsatisfactory, Form 131 sends the appeal to the Indiana Board of Tax Review.

Assessments in 2025 went up by an average of 15% in Wayne County. The assessor pointed to the state's decision to raise cost tables by 30 to 35% across the board, driven by labor and material costs, and noted that 2024 assessments on sold properties averaged about 78% of sale prices.

Form 11 notices had to be in the mail by April 30. A QR code on the notice opened an online appeal, and owners could also download Form 130 or visit the assessor's office. Filing leads to a look at your individual property instead of the mass assessment.

Hold on to a notice showing a big increase. A higher assessment can follow the house into a buyer's costs, and an appeal that is unresolved at closing belongs in a conversation with the title company.

Two installments make up the year, and the 2026 due dates were May 11 and November 10. One bill with both coupons goes out by April 15. Penalties start the day after a due date. Partial payments are welcome at any time, although the full installment is owed by the deadline.

Owners with earlier delinquent taxes pay the 10% rate right away in place of 5%.

sections.h2: What an appeal looks like in practice
sections.html:
1. Open your Form 11 notice and compare its description of the house with the real one, including square footage, finished space and condition.
  2. Choose how to file: scan the code on the notice, print Form 130 or bring it to the assessor.
  3. Back up your case with the sale of a similar house, a repair estimate or photos of damage.
  4. The assessor reviews your property individually. If that does not settle it, a PTABOA hearing comes within 180 days.
  5. You can carry the PTABOA result to the Indiana Board of Tax Review using Form 131.

An appeal addresses the assessed value. It does not touch the rates that local governments set.

Pay at the Treasurer's office, 401 East Main Street, second floor of the Wayne County Annex, phone (765) 973-9238. It opens Monday 8:30 to 5:00 and Tuesday through Friday 8:30 to 4:30. Other ways to pay:

  • Online at taxes.quickviewhere.com with the access code from your bill. The balance shown online omits penalties, so call for the exact amount after a due date.
  • Phone 1-877-690-3729 and give jurisdiction code 2412. Card fees apply.
  • Mail a check, or use the drop box at the Annex, which cannot take cash.
  • Pay in person at a participating bank in the weeks before the spring due date, for a charge of $1 or $2 per parcel that varies by bank.

sections.h2: Can you sell a house with delinquent tax?
sections.html:
Yes. The title company settles the balance out of your sale proceeds. Wayne County's tax sale information runs through sriservices.com, and anyone wanting to redeem a parcel after a sale should speak with the County Auditor.

Phone the treasurer first and ask for the full figure, penalties included, because the online balance leaves them out. Set that number beside the price you expect to net.

We buy houses in Wayne County as-is, whether they carry back taxes, need repairs or have tenants. We make the offer, you decide, and declining costs you nothing.

The county's rules do not stand in the way of a sale. At closing the title company asks the treasurer for the amount due, subtracts it and any mortgage payoff from your proceeds, and records the deed. A cash purchase has no lender, so no appraisal or loan approval delays the date, and the title work sets the pace.

When an installment has come due and gone unpaid, penalties are already building. Say so at the start to the buyer and the title company. The 5% and 10% charges add to the payoff, and you will not see them in the online balance.

The Assessor's office confirms your assessed value and tells you whether an appeal is still possible. The Treasurer quotes a payoff including penalties. The Auditor answers questions about any tax sale touching the parcel.

  1. Locate the latest Form 11 notice and tax bill.
  2. Note the payoff figure and the date it was quoted.
  3. Tell the title company about any appeal still open.
  4. Choose between listing and a direct offer by comparing what you would net after taxes and repairs.

For most sellers the tax piece turns out simpler than they feared. What is owed comes out of the proceeds, and the title company verifies the figure with the county before preparing your closing statement. A seller who has these answers in hand can judge an offer in minutes rather than weeks. Keep the notes together with your deed and any lease, so the title company can answer a buyer's questions without calling you back, and so any penalty or open appeal is explained the same way each time it comes up.

faqs.q: When are Wayne County, Indiana property taxes due?
faqs.a: In 2026 the dates were May 11 and November 10. The treasurer mails one bill by April 15 that carries both coupons.

faqs.q: What are the late penalties in Wayne County?
faqs.a: A late payment draws 5% beginning the day after the due date and 10% roughly 30 days later. Anyone with earlier delinquent taxes pays 10% from the start.

faqs.q: Where is the Wayne County Treasurer?
faqs.a: At 401 East Main Street in Richmond, on the second floor of the Annex Building. The phone number is (765) 973-9238.

faqs.q: How do I appeal a Wayne County assessment?
faqs.a: Send Indiana Form 130 to the Assessor, one per parcel, by June 15 of the right year.

faqs.q: Can I check my Wayne County assessed value online?
faqs.a: Yes. Beacon, the Schneider records site, lets owners look up assessed values.
